title: Technology in Everyday Life
description: Ten short stories about technology in ordinary lives: a senior's first video call, an online order, working from home, phone safety, a map app, old photos, a student app competition, a fitness app, a farm app and a small store that goes online.

lessons.title: Ruth's First Video Call
lessons.summary: Ruth, a senior, learns to make video calls in a free class and starts calling her son's family every weekend.
lessons.text:
Ruth is 79 years old, and she has lived in the same small town in Maine for 50 years. Her son, Mark, lives in California with his wife and their 2 children. The flight from Maine to California is long and expensive, so Ruth takes a flight to see them only once a year.

For many years, Ruth used to call Mark on her old phone every Sunday. She could hear his voice, but she couldn't see the children. "I want to see them, not only hear them," she told her friend Ann.

One day, Ann told Ruth about a free class at the town center. "It's a class for seniors," Ann said. "A young man teaches seniors how to make video calls." Ruth was interested immediately. "I'm very interested," she said. "When does it start?"

The class started the next Monday. There were 8 seniors in the room, and nobody knew much about phones. "Don't worry," said the teacher, Jason. "Nobody knows this at the start. A phone is just a tool for communication, and you already know a lot about communication."

First, Jason showed them the camera on the front of the phone. "This small camera sees you," he explained. "The camera on the back sees the world." Then he showed them how to start a video call. Ruth was practicing with the woman who was sitting next to her when the woman's face appeared on Ruth's screen. "Wow!" Ruth said, and everyone laughed.

That weekend, Ruth called Mark. She was sitting at her table when his face appeared. Then the children ran to the camera. "Wow, we can see you!" they said. Ruth was so happy that she talked to them for an hour.

Since then, Ruth has called her family every weekend. The calls are now a regular part of her week. "This is the best kind of communication," she tells Ann. "And it's much cheaper than a flight!"

Questions:
Where does Ruth's son live?
He lives in California with his wife and their 2 children.
Why does Ruth see her family only once a year?
Because the flight to California is long and expensive.
Who is the class for?
The class is for seniors who want to learn how to make video calls.
How did Ruth feel when she heard about the class?
She was interested immediately.
What did Jason show the seniors first?
He showed them the camera on the front of the phone.
What did Ruth say when she saw the woman's face on her screen?
She said, "Wow!"
How often does Ruth call her family now?
She calls them every weekend, and the calls are a regular part of her week.

lessons.title: A Gift for Mom
lessons.summary: Tom orders a glass bowl online for his mother; it arrives broken, and the store sends a new one.
lessons.text:
Tom wanted to buy a gift for his mother. She loves things made of glass, so he looked for a glass bowl on a shopping website. After an hour, he found a beautiful one. It was blue, and it had the shape of a flower.

The bowl cost $39, plus $6 for shipping. For an additional 75 cents, the store could put it in a gift bag. "75 cents is not much," Tom thought, so he paid the additional cost. The website said that the store would deliver the order in 3 days.

On the third day, Tom was working at home when someone knocked on the door. A man delivered a big box and left. Tom opened the box immediately. The gift bag was inside, but the glass bowl was in 4 pieces. There was no paper around it, so it broke on the way.

Tom took a photo of the broken glass and sent it to the store with a short message: "My order was delivered today, but it was broken. Can you help me?"

One hour later, the store answered. "We are very sorry," the message said. "We will replace it for free. You don't have to send the broken one back." Tom still had some doubt. "What if the new one breaks too?" he thought.

But there was no reason for doubt. 2 days later, a second box was delivered. This time there was a lot of paper inside, and the new bowl was perfect. It had the same flower shape, and it came in a new gift bag. The store replaced the bag too, plus it added a small card that said, "Sorry for the problem!"

On Sunday, Tom gave the gift to his mother. She loved the color and the shape of the bowl. "This is one of the most beautiful gifts I have ever had," she said.

Questions:
What did Tom want to buy?
He wanted to buy a gift for his mother.
What shape did the bowl have?
It had the shape of a flower.
How much did the gift bag cost?
The gift bag cost an additional 75 cents.
What was the problem when the box was delivered?
The glass bowl was in 4 pieces.
What did the store do?
The store replaced the bowl for free.
Why was the second bowl not broken?
Because there was a lot of paper around it.

lessons.title: Anna's Work Diary
lessons.summary: In her diary, Anna writes about her first week of working from home, from a slow internet connection to a good meeting.
lessons.text:
Monday
Today was my first day of working from home. My company has decided that our team will work from home for 3 months. I didn't have to drive to the office, so I had more time for coffee. However, my internet was very slow. Every document took 10 minutes to load. I was waiting for a big document to load when my manager called me. "Why are you so slow today?" he asked. I explained that it wasn't me. It was the internet.

Tuesday
Today I attended 3 online meetings. During the first meeting, nobody could hear me because my sound was off. I won't make that mistake again! The third meeting was with the executive team. The executives wanted to hear about our new project, so I was a little worried. Luckily, the video didn't stop this time.

Wednesday
This morning I got a message from Mrs. Park, our office secretary. She needed a copy of the new agreement with our biggest customer. The agreement was on my computer, but I had to print it, sign it and send a copy back to her. I don't have a printer at home, so I walked to a store near my house. They printed the agreement for me for 50 cents a page.

Thursday
Mrs. Park called me again. She is the best secretary I have ever worked with. She told me that the company was going to transfer $300 to my bank account for a faster internet connection and a good chair. The money arrived in the afternoon, and I ordered both immediately.

Friday
My new internet is much faster than the old one. Now documents load in seconds, not minutes. Today I attended the weekly executive meeting, and everything went well. My manager said that I did a good job with the agreement. I think I'm going to like working from home.

Questions:
Why did documents take so long to load on Monday?
Because Anna's internet was very slow.
What happened during the first meeting on Tuesday?
Nobody could hear Anna because her sound was off.
What did Mrs. Park need on Wednesday?
She needed a copy of the new agreement.
Where did Anna print the agreement?
She printed it at a store near her house.
Why did the company transfer $300 to Anna?
To pay for a faster internet connection and a good chair.

lessons.title: Advice for Dad
lessons.summary: In an email, Kate gives her dad simple advice about safety on his phone after he gets a strange message.
lessons.text:
Hi Dad,

Thank you for calling me last night. You told me that you got a strange message on your phone. The message said, "There is a problem with your bank account. Click this link and type your password." You didn't click the link, and I'm very happy about that. Please don't feel stupid for calling me. Asking questions is never stupid. The stupid thing is to click without thinking.

Messages like that come from people who want to steal your money. First, they try to steal your password. Then they use it to steal money from your account. So here is my advice about safety on your phone.

My first piece of advice is to learn to identify these messages. You can identify them because they usually want you to act immediately. They often say things like "Answer in 1 hour or you will lose your money!" They also often have small mistakes in the words.

My second piece of advice is simple: never give your password to anybody unless you are completely sure who they are. Your bank will never ask for your password in a message. If you are not sure, don't answer unless you have called the bank first. Use the number on the back of your bank card, not the number in the message.

Third, keep the apps on your phone up to date. The new versions are safer than the old ones, and they help prevent many problems.

I really believe that the best defense is knowledge. When you know how these people work, you can prevent most problems yourself. Knowledge is a better defense than any app.

I'm going to visit you this weekend, and I will show you how to keep your phone safe. Your safety is important to me.

Love,
Kate

Questions:
What did the strange message ask Kate's dad to do?
It asked him to click a link and type his password.
Why do people send messages like that?
Because they want to steal money.
How can Dad identify these messages?
They usually want him to act immediately, and they often have small mistakes.
When can Dad give his password to somebody?
He should never give it to anybody unless he is completely sure who they are.
What does Kate think is the best defense?
She thinks that the best defense is knowledge.

lessons.title: The Road to the Beach
lessons.summary: The Lopez family follows a map app to a camp near the beach, but the app sends their old car over too many hills.
lessons.text:
Last summer, the Lopez family drove to a camp near the beach for a week. Carlos was the driver, and his wife, Rosa, sat next to him with her phone. Their 2 children, Leo and Mia, were sitting in the back.

In the past, the family used to use a paper map. Rosa was always the one who read the map, and they often got lost. This time, they had a map app on Rosa's phone. The app had a male voice. "In 500 feet, turn right," said the male voice. Carlos turned right. "This is much easier than a paper map," he said.

The camp was about 300 miles from their home. After the first hundred miles, they stopped for lunch. After the second hundred miles, the app told Carlos to leave the big road. The new road went up a hill and then down again. Then there was another hill, and another.

On the fourth hill, the engine of their old car started to make a strange noise. Carlos stopped the car at the top of the hill. "The engine is too hot," he said. "We have to wait." So they waited for 30 minutes.

While they were waiting, Rosa looked at the settings of the map app, and she found the problem. The app was showing them the shortest road, not the easiest one. She changed the settings, and the map showed a new road with no more hills. It was a little longer, but it was much better for an old engine.

3 hours later, they arrived at the camp. It was in the woods, only a few minutes from the beach. Their small house at the camp was made of wood, and it smelled like trees. The children ran to the beach immediately.

That evening, the family sat on the beach and watched the sun go down. "Next time," Carlos said, "I will look at the map before we leave."

Questions:
Who was the driver?
Carlos was the driver.
What kind of voice did the map app have?
The app had a male voice.
When did the family stop for lunch?
They stopped for lunch after the first hundred miles.
What happened on the fourth hill?
The engine started to make a strange noise.
How did Rosa fix the problem?
She changed the settings of the map app.
Where was the camp?
It was in the woods, only a few minutes from the beach.

lessons.title: A Phone Full of Memories
lessons.summary: Lily helps her grandfather free the memory on his phone, and they choose photos for a book about 50 years of marriage.
lessons.text:
My grandfather, Joe, is 76 years old, and he loves his phone. He takes photos of everything: his garden, his food and, most of all, his cat, Max. Next month, Joe and Helen, his wife, are going to celebrate 50 years of marriage. Joe wants to give Helen a special gift: a book of photos from their life together.

Last Saturday, Joe called me. "Lily, my phone says that the memory is full," he said. "I can't take any more photos. Can you help me?" I went to his house that afternoon.

We sat down together and looked at his photos. Soon we discovered more than 3,000 photos of the cat! There were photos of the cat sleeping, the cat eating and the cat looking out the window. "This is a waste of memory," I told him. "You don't need 3,000 photos of one cat. Let's not waste any more memory on him." Joe laughed. "I know. But he is a very good cat." We kept the best 50 cat photos and deleted the rest.

Then we looked at Joe's old photos, which he moved onto his phone from his old computer years ago. There we discovered a photo of the day Joe and Helen got married, in 1975. Joe was wearing a black suit and a tie, and Helen was wearing a white dress. "I knew I wanted to marry her the first time I saw her," Joe said. "I asked her to marry me after 3 months."

I asked Joe why he loved this photo so much. "I'm not good at expressing my feelings with words," he said. "But this photo expresses everything. It's my favorite memory."

We spent the rest of the afternoon choosing photos for the book. We chose a photo from every year of their marriage. Then we ordered the book online, and I put the photo with the black suit and the tie on the first page.

Joe was very happy. "This book is better than any memory on my phone," he said. "And now I have space for more photos of the cat!"

Questions:
What are Joe and Helen going to celebrate next month?
They are going to celebrate 50 years of marriage.
What was the problem with Joe's phone?
The memory was full.
What did Lily and Joe discover on the phone?
They discovered more than 3,000 photos of the cat.
What was Joe wearing on the day he married Helen?
He was wearing a black suit and a tie.
Why does Joe love the photo so much?
Because it expresses everything, and it is his favorite memory.

lessons.title: The App Competition
lessons.summary: Sara's team builds an app that helps families waste less food and wins their college competition.
lessons.text:
Sara is a student at a college in Texas. This year, she is taking a class about making phone apps. Her professor, Dr. Moss, has developed more than 20 apps herself. She is the best professor Sara has ever had.

In the first weeks, the class studied theory. "In theory, making an app is easy," Professor Moss said. "In practice, it is much harder." Then she told the class about a competition. Every team of 3 students had to make an app that helps people in their town. The best app would be the winner, and the winner's team would get $1,000. The competition was also part of their grade.

Sara worked with her friends Omar and Jen. First, they did an analysis of the problems in their town. They asked a hundred people questions about their lives. The analysis showed that many families throw away a lot of food. So the team chose a mission: to help families waste less food.

For 2 months, the team worked every evening. They developed an app that tells you which food in your house will go bad soon. It also shows simple ways to cook that food. Professor Moss had a big influence on their work. Her advice was always short and clear: "Make it simple."

On the day of the competition, 15 teams showed their apps to 3 judges. The judges ranked all the apps from 1 to 15. Sara's team was ranked first, so they were the winners!

At the end of the class, Sara got the highest grade. "Professor Moss had a big influence on me," Sara said later. "Because of her, I want to make apps that help people."

Questions:
Who is Professor Moss?
She is Sara's professor, and she has developed more than 20 apps.
What did the teams have to make for the competition?
They had to make an app that helps people in their town.
What did the analysis show?
It showed that many families throw away a lot of food.
What was the mission of Sara's team?
Their mission was to help families waste less food.
How did the judges rank Sara's team?
They ranked it first, so Sara's team was the winner.
What grade did Sara get?
She got the highest grade.

lessons.title: Ben's Fitness App
lessons.summary: Ben, who used to smoke, uses a fitness app that wakes him up, tells him how to exercise and helps him cook better food.
lessons.text:
Ben is 45 years old. He used to smoke every day, but he stopped smoking a year ago. "Stopping smoking was the best thing I have ever done," he says. Now he wants to be even healthier, so he has put a fitness app on his phone.

Every morning, the app wakes Ben up at 6 with soft music. Before the app, he used to wake up at 8 and feel tired all day. Now he wakes up early and goes to the bathroom to wash his face with cold water. Then he goes to the living room for his exercise.

The app has a woman's voice that tells Ben what to do. "Raise your arms over your head," the voice says. Ben raises his arms. "Now jump 20 times." Ben jumps. "Good. Now raise your right arm, then your left arm." Ben does everything the voice says. At first, the jumps were difficult for him, but now they are easier.

The app also helps Ben with food. It shows him how to cook healthy meals. Ben never used to cook. He used to buy fast food. Now he cooks fish and rice 3 times a week. The app also tells him to eat fewer sweet things. Ben loves sweet food, so this is the hardest part. Now he eats something sweet only on Sundays.

After 3 months, Ben feels much better. He has lost 15 pounds, and he has more energy. One morning, he was washing his face in the bathroom when he noticed that his skin looked better too. "Your skin looks great," his sister told him later. "Is it because you stopped smoking?" "It's because of everything," Ben said. "No smoking, better food and a lot of jumping!"

Questions:
What did Ben use to do every day?
He used to smoke every day.
What time does the app wake Ben up?
It wakes him up at 6.
What does the voice tell Ben to do?
It tells him to raise his arms and jump.
What does the app show Ben about food?
It shows him how to cook healthy meals.
When does Ben eat something sweet now?
He eats something sweet only on Sundays.
How does Ben feel after 3 months?
He feels much better, and his skin looks better too.

lessons.title: Henry's Farm App
lessons.summary: Henry tries an app that tells him when to water his fields, and he saves water and money on his farm.
lessons.text:
Henry Clark has a farm in Iowa. His family has had the farm for more than 100 years. Henry's father and his father's father worked on the same farm, and they did everything by hand and by experience.

For a farm, water is one of the most important factors. The weather is another important factor. In the past, Henry generally decided when to water his fields by looking at the sky. But in the last few years, the summers have become hotter and drier, particularly in July and August. Henry was using more and more water, and the cost was going up.

Last year, Henry's daughter, Amy, told him about a farm app. Small machines in the fields measure how much water is in the ground. The app shows this information on the phone and tells the farmer when to water. "It's an investment," Amy said. "But it's a relatively small investment." The machines and the app cost $3,000. For a farm, that is relatively cheap.

Henry had some doubts because the majority of farmers in his area generally don't use apps for their work. Still, he decided to try.

The results were significant. In the first summer, Henry used 30 percent less water. The difference was particularly big in July, the hottest month. He saved more than $5,000. For Henry, that was a significant amount of money.

Henry used part of the money for the construction of a new building for his animals. The construction took 2 months, and his neighbors came to help. Now some of his neighbors are interested in the app too. "It was the best investment I have ever made," Henry tells them.

Questions:
How long has Henry's family had the farm?
They have had the farm for more than 100 years.
How did Henry generally decide when to water his fields?
He generally decided by looking at the sky.
Why did Henry have some doubts?
Because the majority of farmers in his area generally don't use apps for their work.
How much did the machines and the app cost?
They cost $3,000.
What were the results in the first summer?
Henry used 30 percent less water and saved more than $5,000.
What did Henry use part of the money for?
He used it for the construction of a new building for his animals.

lessons.title: Nina's Store Goes Online
lessons.summary: Nina, who owns a small independent store, tries a free website service and starts selling her books far beyond her city.
lessons.text:
Nina owns a small independent store in Portland that sells books and cards. It is not part of a big company, and Nina makes all the decisions herself. For 10 years, the store did well. But recently, more and more people have started to buy their books on big commercial websites.

"You need to sell online too," her friend Kim told her. "It's absolutely necessary today." Nina wasn't sure. "Those big commercial websites have hundreds of workers," she said. "I'm only one person." "You don't need hundreds of workers," Kim said. "You just need a simple website."

Kim told Nina about a service that helps small stores make their own websites. It had a free trial for 30 days. "Try it," Kim said. "If you don't like it, stop after the trial." So Nina started the free trial that evening.

Making the website was easier than she expected. She added photos of her books, wrote short notes about each one and put in the prices. Then she announced the new website on the store's social media page. She also put a sign in the window. "Our store is now online!" the sign announced.

The first orders came from people in Portland. But soon, orders came from beyond the city, and then from beyond the state. One week, a man in Japan ordered 3 books. "My store is global now!" Nina said with a laugh.

Now Nina maintains the website herself. Every evening, she spends an hour updating it. Maintaining a website takes time, but it is absolutely worth it. When the trial ended, she paid for the full service immediately. "My store is still independent," she says. "Now it's just bigger."

Questions:
What does Nina's store sell?
It sells books and cards.
What did Kim tell Nina?
She told Nina that she needed to sell online too.
How long was the free trial?
The free trial was for 30 days.
How did Nina tell people about the new website?
She announced it on the store's social media page and put a sign in the window.
Where did the orders come from?
They came from Portland, and then from beyond the city and the state.
Why did Nina say that her store was global?
Because a man in Japan ordered 3 books.
What does Nina do every evening?
She maintains the website for an hour.
